cases.name: Lara Beth Sweat
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Lara was born in Urbana, IL, on December 9, 1968, and raised in San Diego, CA, and Downingtown, PA. Lara earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University in 1990 and a Juris Doctor from Widener University, where she was a member of Law Review in 1998. After moving to the San Francisco area in 1999 and eventually settling in Oakland, Lara practiced law in California for nine years, seven of those with the California Department of Insurance. A dedicated professional, she was respected by colleagues and opponents alike. Forever thinking of others, she was an ideal friend. Always protective of her brothers, she was a model for all big sisters. Yet what Lara clearly loved above all was being a mother. Her two children meant the world to her, and making a joyful home for them was the great passion of her life. For all who knew her, the sun now shines a little less brightly and music sounds a little less sweet. The wit, humor, energy, spirit and style in which she embraced life will live on in her children. "i carry your heart with me (i carry it in my heart) i am never without it (anywhere i go you go, my dear...)" - ee cummings"
cases.narrative: Eric Basuino reportedly shot his wife, Laura Sweat, as she tried to escape when police came to the door, then retreated to the back of the house and killed himself.

cases.name: Grace Eunhea Kim
cases.about: She was a student at Oikos University's nursing school who worked as a waitress at BJ's Restaurant and Brewhouse in Newark. James Villanueva, 22, of Newark, was one of her co-workers at BJ's. "She was full of life. She truly was the life of the party," Villanueva said. He described her playful personality and how she would use the intercom at work to sing and joke with co-workers. "She was very confident, energetic and ecstatic about everything," Villanueva said. Kim's friends expressed their grief and shock on Facebook and Twitter, describing her as bubbly and humorous, beautiful and fun.

She was a student at Montera Middle School.

"She was a very kind person. She wasn’t rude or nothing. She was there for people," said Denise. "She loved braiding hair. She was good at it."

"She wanted to do better in her life and get things right and show was struggling with some things. She loved her children. This I know for sure," Patton said.
